item.description:
Shelves no longer leave their first book standing up.

  • Fixed: after clicking a shelf, its first book stayed lifted with its title showing, even with the pointer elsewhere. The keyboard highlight now shows only once you use the arrow keys or Tab to the shelf.
  • A long shelf (in the Catalogue's shelf view or a category) keeps one height as you scroll it, sized for its tallest book, instead of depending on which books are on screen.

Today leads with what you're reading, the Catalogue gains shelves, kinds include Textbook and your own, and the reader's controls live in Aa and Info.

  • New: Textbook is one of the kinds a piece can be.
  • New: Settings ▸ Library ▸ Kinds lets you add kinds of your own, such as Lecture notes or Zine. They appear in a piece's details and in the Catalogue's filters; renaming one renames it on its pieces, and deleting one returns its pieces to Article, PDF or EPUB.
  • Today's big headline is now the piece you're reading (the last one you opened that's begun and not finished), marked "Continue reading". With nothing in progress it shows the top of your stack, as before.
  • New: switch the Catalogue between List and Shelf. Shelf sets every piece out as spines, one shelf per group in the arrangement you've chosen (A to Z, by length, newest), with the same search, filters and right-click actions. List stays the default.
  • The reader's "…" menu is gone. Its actions (the stack, favourite, rename, export highlights, the cover and delete) are now in Info, under Actions, beside the details they belong with.
  • A PDF's notes column is switched on and off in Aa, under Notes (⇧⌘A still works).
  • With keyboard navigation turned on in System Settings, the focused button, tab, filter or Aa control now shows a clear outline in Scribe's accent colour, distinct from hover and selection.

Reading stays offline and private, each book keeps to its own files, and Scribe tells you when something couldn't be saved.

  • Reading is fully offline and private: an article image that didn't save, or a web image, font or stylesheet a book asks for, is no longer fetched when you open it. Scribe keeps trying to save missing images in the background.
  • Images that couldn't be saved are hidden rather than shown broken.
  • An open book can read only its own files: not the other books in your library, and not the web.
  • The reader keeps no cookies or website data between pieces.
  • Problems with saving, the library and housekeeping are written to the Mac's system log, so they can be looked into later without exposing what you read: links, titles, notes and error details are kept private.
  • If a highlight, note, tag, category, stack change or other edit can't be saved, a bar under the top bar says so, instead of it quietly not happening.
  • A note that can't be saved keeps its editor open with what you wrote.
  • Exporting highlights to a place that can't be written to now says so.
